fatal_errors: The hypothesis does not identify the tested AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy and instead proposes an unspecified Cr/Mo-containing optimized HEA; molybdenum is not part of the target alloy.
It omits the defining L12/B2 lamellar dual-phase microstructure and its retention after rapid thermal cycling.
It does not reconstruct the comparison with duplex stainless steel 2205 under immersed reciprocating tribo-corrosion in deionized water.
The proposed solid-solution explanation is inaccurate for the target material, whose performance depends on a stable dual-phase eutectic microstructure, passivation and tribo-layer repair.
The cited evidence concerns irradiation, refractory HEAs, oxidation, or molten-salt corrosion rather than the target aqueous elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion experiment.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad idea that an HEA may outperform conventional structural alloys and mentions protective oxides, but it does not recover the specific material, comparator, experimental conditions, temperature-dependent wear minimum near 50 °C, or measured outcomes. Its emphasis on generic Cr/Mo composition optimization is not the intervention studied and introduces Mo incorrectly. Although the proposed comparative experiment is directionally relevant, it lacks controlled temperature, load, frequency, electrochemical monitoring, and wear-volume measurements needed to discriminate the target mechanism. The cited literature offers only indirect plausibility and does not validate the stated tribo-corrosion conclusion.
